text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two applications to communicate with each other. To get data, you send HTTP requests to a server, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with JSON, a simple text format that is easy to read and parse. Before you can access the data, you usually need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. Many APIs also have rate limits, which means you can only send a certain number of requests per minute. Finally, always add error handling to your code, because requests can fail for many reasons, such as a lost connection or an invalid key.
